data.title: Market Regroups After Huge Rally to Start the Week
data.description:
U.S. equities are rising slightly in the futures market after a huge rally to begin the trading week. Stocks surged on Nov. 23 after Nvidia (NVDA) reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, with the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index closing 6% higher. Data from TipRanks shows that the benchmark S&P 500 index gained 4.73% on the day and the blue-chip Dow added 3%. It was the best day for the U.S. market since April 2025.

Nvidia's stock soared 32% on news that the company's board of directors returned Huang as the head of the company, effective immediately. Huang had resigned earlier in November after admitting to an affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Other stocks associated with the AI trade jumped sharply higher on news of Huang's return, with Micron Technology (MU) rising 19% and CoreWeave (CRWV) jumping 22%.

In the futures pits, the Nasdaq is unchanged, while the S&P 500 is up 0.08%, and the Dow is gaining 0.03%.

Above is a chart from TipRanks that shows the year-to-date performance of Nvidia's stock. As one can see, NVDA shares have declined 33% in 2026.

Oil Falls and Gold Rises

Elsewhere in the market, the price of crude oil fell sharply on Nov. 23 while the price of gold rallied. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil, the U.S. standard, dropped 3% on the day to close at $80.38 per barrel. Brent crude oil, the international benchmark, also fell 3% and finished trading at $89.46 a barrel. Oil prices moved lower after U.S. President Donald Trump said he has no plans to continue the Iran war, according to a report in The Wall Street Journal.

As oil prices moved lower, gold rose to start the week. The price of bullion ended the trading session up 3.34% at $3,633.10 per ounce. At one point, gold's price was up as much as 5%. The jump in gold's price comes after a steep selloff in recent months. After hitting an all-time high of $5,608 per ounce in January, gold's price had declined about 30% this year prior to the latest increase, according to data from TipRanks.

Other metals also rose to begin the trading week. The price of silver increased 4% to close at $42.90 per ounce. Copper's price gained 2% on the day and prices for platinum and palladium each rose by more than 2%. Metals are benefitting from dip buying among investors and expectations for less aggressive interest rate hikes from the U.S. Federal Reserve.

Is NVDA Stock a Buy?

Nvidia's stock has a consensus Moderate Buy rating among 44 Wall Street analysts. That rating is based on 31 Buy, 12 Hold, and one Sell recommendations issued in the past three months. The average NVDA price target of $231.51 implies 36% upside from current levels.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: 3 Technology ETFs That Can Deliver 25%+ Gains
data.description:
The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH), Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT), and Fidelity MSCI Information Technology Index ETF (FTEC) are three technology exchange-traded funds (ETFs) with more than 25% upside potential, according to Wall Street analysts' average price targets for their holdings.

Technology stocks have been volatile due to concerns about the durability of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade and macro pressures. Leadership turmoil at Nvidia (NVDA) also affected investor sentiment. However, AI and tech stocks rallied on Monday, as Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.

Despite the ongoing volatility, investors remain interested in capitalizing on the long-term growth potential of tech companies in areas such as AI, cloud computing, quantum computing, semiconductors, and cybersecurity. Tech ETFs help investors gain diversified exposure to attractive stocks while mitigating company-specific risks.

VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH)

The SMH ETF tracks the MVIS US Listed Semiconductor 25 Index and includes stocks of companies involved in semiconductor production and equipment. It is suitable for investors who want to capitalize on the strong growth opportunities of semiconductor companies, which are seeing robust demand from the ongoing AI wave.

According to TipRanks' unique ETF analyst consensus, determined based on a weighted average of analyst ratings on its holdings, SMH scores a Strong Buy rating. The average price target of $623.04 for the SMH ETF implies 35.4% upside potential.

Currently, the top three holdings of the SMH ETF are Nvidia (NVDA), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM), and Broadcom (AVGO). Overall, SMH has about $59.2 billion in assets under management (AUM).

Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT)

The VGT ETF tracks the MSCI U.S. IMI 25/50 Information Technology Index and comprises stocks of companies in the electronics and computer industries or that manufacture products based on the latest applied science.

Based on a weighted average of analyst ratings on its holdings, VGT earns a Strong Buy rating. The average price target of $135.43 for the VGT ETF implies about 27.3% upside potential.

Currently, the top three holdings of the VGT ETF are Apple (AAPL), Nvidia, and Microsoft (MSFT). Overall, VGT has about $131.3 billion in AUM, way higher than the other two technology ETFs discussed here.

Fidelity MSCI Information Technology Index ETF (FTEC)

The FTEC ETF tracks the MSCI USA IMI Information Technology Index and is suitable for investors seeking exposure to rapid advancements and growth in the technology sector. It includes tech giants and innovative companies across sub-sectors such as software, hardware, semiconductors, and IT services. 

Based on a weighted average of analyst ratings on its holdings, FTEC earns a Moderate Buy rating. The average price target of $318.53 for the FTEC ETF implies about 25.4% upside potential.

The top three holdings of the FTEC ETF are Apple, Nvidia, and Microsoft. FTEC ETF has about $19 billion in AUM.

data.title: Is Lululemon (LULU) a Buy Ahead of Black Friday?
data.description:
Lululemon (LULU) has shed 50% year-to-date amid heightened competition from Alo and Vuori, although the athleisure apparel company has two major catalysts in store. The first is Black Friday on November 27, which could help boost sales as shoppers take advantage of major discounts. The second is the company's upcoming earnings report, which is estimated to be on December 10.

Black Friday is one of Lululemon's biggest shopping events of the year, with customers in search of deals on its popular leggings, hoodies, and other clothing items. The company has historically offered discounts of around 30% on select items during the event. Strong holiday demand could help Lululemon clear its inventory and attract new customers. At the same time, investors will also be watching whether discounts put pressure on profit margins.

Wall Street Awaits Lululemon's Earnings

Rising energy costs stemming from the U.S.-Iran war have pressured the margins of apparel companies. Higher energy costs make it more expensive for these companies to make and ship clothing. These added expenses can eat into profits if companies can't pass the higher costs on to customers. "But we do think corporates are going to try and pass through prices to offset some of the raw material increases that they are going to see next year," said Goldman Sachs Consumer Sector Specialist Scott Feiler.

Meanwhile, Wall Street expects Lululemon to report revenue of $2.31 billion and an adjusted EPS of $1.04 for the third quarter. History suggests that the company will post a beat on earnings, as it has surpassed estimates for 19 consecutive quarters. Still, margins, revenue, guidance, and comparable sales will matter just as much as earnings.

Should You Buy LULU Stock?

Wall Street believes that LULU stock should be priced lower. During the past three months, analysts have issued an average LULU price target of $100.73, implying downside of 3.82% from current prices. The highest price target sits at $169, while the lowest is at $44. Of the 28 analysts covering LULU, one rates it a Buy, 22 rate it a Hold, and five rate it a Sell.
data.author: Eddie Pan

data.title: Nasdaq Closes 6% Higher After Jensen Huang Returns as Nvidia's CEO
data.description:
U.S. stocks surged into the close on Nov. 23 after Nvidia (NVDA) reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, with the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index rising 7% and regaining much of the losses from last Friday. News of Huang's return reignited the artificial intelligence (AI) trade and pushed every major U.S. index higher to start the trading week.

The Nasdaq added 1,563 points to close up 6.92%. The benchmark S&P 500 index gained 5.03% on the day, and the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 1,556 points, or 3.21%. It was the best day for each of the three major American averages since April 2025 when U.S. President Donald Trump scaled back his tariff regime.

NVDA Stock Skyrockets

Nvidia's stock was the big winner on the day, soaring 33% on news that the company's board of directors returned Huang as the head of the company, effective immediately. Huang had resigned earlier this month after admitting to a number of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.

Other stocks associated with the AI trade jumped sharply higher on news of Huang's return as Nvidia's CEO. Shares of Micron Technology (MU) rose 19%, while CoreWeave (CRWV) increased 20%. The stock of Nvidia rival Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) gained 6%, while the stocks of hyperscalers Alphabet (GOOGL) and Meta Platforms (META) each rose more than 5%.

A Big Reversal on Wall Street

The big gains on Nov. 23 marked a big reversal for technology stocks following last Friday's massive selloff as worries about the AI trade spooked investors. On Nov. 20, the Nasdaq index fell 5% and gave up all of its gains on the year. The S&P 500 and Dow ended last week in a correction, defined as a decline of 10% or more from recent highs.

Value stocks, or shares of companies seen as a safe havens in times of market turmoil, did not fare well on Nov. 23 as investors rotated money back into the AI sector. Shares of Costco Wholesale (COST) and Coca-Cola (KO) each declined about 1%. This is a shortened trading week, with U.S. markets closed on Nov. 26 for the Thanksgiving holiday. The trading session on Nov. 27 will be shortened with the closing bell taking place at 1 p.m. in New York rather than 4 p.m.

Stock Winners and Losers

Stocks that led the market rally on Nov. 23 include:

  • Nvidia (NVDA)
  • Dell (DELL)
  • Micron Technology (MU)
  • Marvell (MRVL)
  • Nebius Group (NBIS)

Stocks that underperformed to begin the trading week include:

  • Chevron (CVX)
  • UnitedHealth (UNH)
  • Johnson & Johnson (JNJ)
  • Coca-Cola (KO)
  • CrowdStrike (CRWD)

data.title: Elon Musk's Skydance Connection Leads Skydance Stock (NYSE:SKYD) Up
data.description:
Entertainment giant Skydance (SKYD) recently brought on a new investor in the form of Tesla (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk, who added around a billion dollars to Skydance's coffers. This immediately got people wondering just what Musk would get out of the deal. New reports from The Street suggest some possibilities. Skydance stock gained over 3% in the closing minutes of Monday's trading. Skydance has seen a 58.83% loss in its share price over the past year.

Musk's Deal

It was immediately clear that Musk—and his money—were welcome at Skydance. David Ellison referred to Elon as "the greatest entrepreneur of our time," and further noted, "I have so much admiration and respect for Elon." Tesla "…doesn't invest in a lot of companies," Ellison noted as well. But that left the question of why Elon would put that kind of money behind a studio.

One potential avenue is a connection with Starlink. The satellite network could partner with Skydance—and its two streaming platforms that will eventually be one—to offer some kind of bundle package. Given the expense of Starlink—though the service does offer excellent speeds and uptime, as I have been personally using it for months now—offering some kind of bundle plan might be particularly useful in getting some subscribers on board. This is particularly true in areas where there are multiple options for internet access.

Letting Gunn Go a Bad Plan?

A report from The Signal suggests that Skydance might have made a serious miscalculation in letting James Gunn go. And while Gunn was actually glad to go in some respects—Gunn noted that the corporate part of his job was remarkably difficult and left him little time for himself—the loss of Gunn as part of the DC universe is potentially a serious problem.

Some say that Gunn's at least partial removal—he still has some projects in the works at Skydance, though there may not be future ones around—was a matter of taste. New hire Jeremy Latcham is said to be focused on making "…hits for the masses…" and has the "broader" tastes that line up with David Ellison's own. This in turn is likely to contribute to "superhero fatigue," which had been wearing the entire industry down to some extent, the report notes.

Is Skydance a Good Stock to Buy Now?

data.title: Nvidia Stock (NVDA) Soars on Jensen Huang's Return as CEO; Analysts React Positively
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) stock rallied more than 30% on Monday after the semiconductor company's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Huang resigned on November 12 following reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. intelligence officials allege is a Chinese spy. Like investors, several Wall Street analysts welcomed the news of Huang's return. Notably, Melius Research, Bernstein, StoneX, and Oppenheimer upgraded their ratings on NVDA stock to Buy from Hold.

Many analysts reaffirmed their Buy rating on NVDA stock following the news. For instance, Stifel analyst Rubey Roy reiterated a Buy rating on NVDA stock with a price target of $205, saying that Huang's return removed a "key-person overhang" on the company's AI infrastructure roadmap, which includes the launch of Vera Rubin Ultra in 2027 and Feynman in 2028, as well as on recent supplier commitments.

For Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), the 5-star analyst doesn't see any significant impact, as its "second-source case" is driven by supply constraints and not leadership disruption at Nvidia.

StoneX Upgrades Nvidia Stock to Buy

StoneX analyst Cody Acree upgraded Nvidia stock to Buy from Hold with a price target of $270. The 5-star analyst noted the board's statement that it is satisfied with Huang's "candor and ability to lead" Nvidia. The board also said that based on input from senior levels of the U.S. government, it is confident that Huang's return "poses no national security risk."

Acree said that Huang's reinstatement reverses most of his concerns that drove his November 12 rating downgrade. The analyst specified the downgrade was about the multiple, not his estimates. Notably, the analyst is now encouraged that Huang's return to Nvidia addresses five key issues:

  • Pace of the product roadmap
  • Nvidia's industry relationships
  • Willingness to support AI infrastructure buildout
  • Maintenance of the company's organizational structure
  • Retention of key talent

With the interim team ensuring to be "disciplined and selective," Acree expects Huang to use Nvidia's financial strength to support neocloud and frontier-lab customers, which should help drive much of the company's out-year growth.

Meanwhile, Acree warned investors about two "open" risks – the board's investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort and the November 19 Department of Commerce's rule that requires licenses for advanced chips shipped to five additional countries and for any data center that gives China-based companies significant compute. Acree highlighted that each gigawatt of regional capacity that cannot be licensed represents 3% to 5% of his FY28 revenue estimate, with the risk expected to grow in FY29.

Is NVDA a Good Stock to Buy Now?

Currently, Wall Street has a Moderate Buy consensus rating on Nvidia stock based on 32 Buys, 11 Holds, and one Sell. The average NVDA stock price target of $232.39 indicates 41.1% upside potential.

These ratings and price targets could change as more analysts react to Huang's return.
data.author: Sirisha Bhogaraju

data.title: Invesco QQQ ETF Jumps 7% as Jensen Huang's Nvidia Comeback Fuels AI Stock Rally
data.description:
Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq-100 index (NDX), climbed 7% to about $651 on Monday afternoon. This erased Friday's 5.67% decline, triggered by a sell-off in AI chip stocks. As of the time of writing, Nvidia shares (NVDA) were up 31% to about $164, adding about $1 trillion to the AI chipmaker's market capitalization. This followed Nvidia's announcement that it had reinstated co-founder and longtime leader Jensen Huang as CEO.

The news triggered a rally in AI and tech stocks. This pushed the Nasdaq-100 up by about 7% in Monday afternoon trading. It followed a bruising session for the index on Friday amid a broad market meltdown.

Of note, Nvidia is the third-largest holding in the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF. The chipmaker weighs 5.57%. It is led only by Apple (AAPL) at 9.21% and Microsoft (MSFT) at 6.63%.

Which Other Stocks Helped to Power QQQ's Rally?

While tech stocks traded up on Monday afternoon, certain companies among QQQ's top holdings rallied more. These stocks added momentum to Nvidia's broad rally and helped to power QQQ higher.

  • As of the time of writing, Micron shares (MU) surged about 18% to around $701. Huang's return as Nvidia CEO helped ease investors' recent anxiety about future memory chip supplies. MU shares have been under pressure after Huang's resignation less than two weeks ago. This is due to worries about Nvidia's future spending plans. The development matters to investors as Micron's high-speed memory chips are usually paired with Nvidia's GPUs in data centers to power massive AI workloads.
  • Tesla shares (TSLA) jumped by 12% to about $387. This came after a four-star JPMorgan analyst Rajat Gupta commented on the electric car maker's latest Full Self-Driving software. Gupta noted that the technology shows Tesla remains ahead of competitors.
  • Shares in tech companies Meta (META) and Alphabet (GOOGL) were also up about 7% as of the time of writing. The shares gained amid the the rally.
  • Chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is also worth mentioning. It rose 6% to $448. This came after five-star Bernstein analyst Mark Newman continued to back the company despite the recent attack from a short seller.

Is QQQ a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

The Invesco QQQ Trust ETF has a Strong Buy rating. This reflects TipRanks' unique ETF analyst consensus. This method relies on a weighted average of analyst ratings on the fund's holdings.

In addition, the average QQQ price target of $882.06 suggests about 35% upside.
data.author: Solomon Oladipupo

data.title: Is Huang's Nvidia Return the Market Bottom? Here's What Wall Street Thinks
data.description:
Is the stock market correction finally over? Some Wall Street strategists believe it could be after chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA) reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday, which sent its shares up by more than 30%. Indeed, the Nasdaq 100 surged by nearly 7%. The rebound came after all three major indexes ended Friday in correction territory by having fallen more than 10% from their recent highs. However, analysts remain divided over whether Monday's rally is a lasting recovery.

According to CNBC, Mark Gibbens, founder of Gibbens Capital Management, believes that Huang's return could establish a bottom for AI stocks. His argument is that Nvidia plays such an important role in the AI industry that restoring confidence in its leadership could help stabilize the market.

Meanwhile, Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth, believes that stocks may have already reached a bottom before Monday's announcement. He pointed to Friday's widespread selling as a sign that the market had become oversold. In fact, stock futures were already higher Sunday night before Nvidia announced Huang's return.

Hogan also noted that technology stocks were trading at 16.3 times expected earnings, compared to 20.5 times for consumer staples. He argued that this gap was difficult to justify since the technology sector's earnings outlook is stronger.

Why Other Wall Street Strategists Remain Cautious

Despite Monday's rally, Freedom Capital Markets strategist Jay Woods believes that the recovery could fade. He is concerned that Huang's return does little to resolve the problems that caused AI stocks to decline in the first place.

Those problems include uncertainty over whether major technology companies will continue spending heavily on AI infrastructure. There are also worries that stricter approval requirements for new data centers could delay construction projects.

Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at One Point BFG Wealth Partners, has similar doubts. He argues that companies supplying AI infrastructure remain heavily dependent on how much their customers spend.

This is especially important for Nvidia, which reported quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, a 103% increase from a year earlier. Although the company expects revenue of about $130 billion in the current quarter, Boockvar believes that the longer-term performance of AI hardware suppliers will depend on whether major technology companies maintain their spending plans.

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on Nvidia stock based on 32 Buys, 11 Holds, and one Sell assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. Furthermore, the average Nvidia price target of $232.39 per share implies 39.8% upside potential. (See NVDA Stock Forecast).
